turns.prompt_text: Does there exist a portable scanner? I know I can scan documents using my phone but it takes so long and if I had a lot of pages to go through it would take a lot of time
turns.response_html:
Yes, portable scanners definitely exist, and they are much faster than using a phone because they eliminate the need to manually align, focus, and flip every single page.

If you are dealing with a high volume of documents, you’ll want to look for a portable sheet-fed scanner with an Automatic Document Feeder (ADF). These allow you to drop a stack of papers into a tray, and the scanner will pull them through automatically.

Top Portable Scanners for High Volumes

Depending on how much space you have and how "portable" you need it to be, here are the best options currently available:

1. The Compact Workhorse: Ricoh ScanSnap iX1300

This is often considered the "gold standard" for portable bulk scanning. It's small enough to fit on a corner of a desk or in a backpack, but it features a 20-page ADF.

  • Speed: Approximately 30 pages per minute.
  • Key Feature: It has a unique "U-turn" path for standard documents (saving space) and a "Return" path for thick items like IDs or embossed cards.

2. The Truly Mobile Choice: Epson WorkForce ES-300W

If you need something that doesn't even require a wall outlet, this is a top-tier choice.

  • Power: Runs on a built-in battery and connects via Wi-Fi.
  • ADF: Holds up to 20 sheets at a time.
  • Speed: Scans both sides of a page simultaneously (Duplex) at about 25 pages per minute.

3. The "Light" Budget Option: Brother ADS-1800W

A great middle-ground that offers a 2.8-inch color touchscreen and a 20-sheet feeder. It's powered via USB-C, so you can run it directly off your laptop.

Why a Scanner Beats a Phone App

While phone apps are convenient for a single receipt, they struggle with volume for several reasons:

FeaturePhone ScanningPortable ADF Scanner
Speed15–30 seconds per page (manual)2–4 seconds per page (automatic)
ConsistencyRisk of "warped" or "tilted" imagesFixed internal sensors ensure flat, straight scans
DuplexingMust flip page and scan againScans both sides in a single pass
FatigueHigh (holding phone, lining up shots)Low (load tray and press "Go")

A Quick Tip on "Wand" Scanners

You may see "wand" scanners (where you manually slide the device over the paper). Avoid these for high volumes. They are often slower and more frustrating than your phone because any slight hand tremor causes the image to distort. Stick to sheet-fed models for the speed you're looking for.
